title: Why Indian hockey team jersey changed from blue to saffron: HI explains
content: Hockey India will use saffron jerseys for the 2026 World Cup. According to Hockey India, the traditional blue jersey blended with the blue artificial turf used in international hockey, making it difficult for players to spot teammates during matches. The federation said players and coaches suggested different colours before saffron was chosen.

title: US Senator introduces bill he calls 'commonsense fix to outdated immigration system'
content: Senator Alex Padilla introduced a bill offering a green card pathway.  This proposal would benefit millions of long-term immigrants residing in the US.  It updates an outdated immigration law provision from 1929.  The bill requires seven years of continuous residency and no criminal record.  This legislation aims to provide certainty for contributing residents.

title: Jointly property ownership: What happens when co-owners disagree over rent or sale
content: A growing number of buyers are opting for shared homeownership to alleviate financial strain and share loan obligations. In various states, including a woman as a co-owner can unlock potential stamp duty reductions. However, this arrangement necessitates mutual consent for the sale of the property and any loan matters, with each co-owner entitled to sell their respective portion. Disputes between co-owners can result in negotiations, buyouts, or legal partitions.

title: Why a chicken biryani demand for Tamil Nadu schools is making headlines across India
content: In Tamil Nadu, the noon-meal initiative is exploring the addition of chicken biryani to its menu, reflecting an evolution in its commitment to student welfare. Teachers have also addressed unresolved issues related to employment conditions and salaries. Furthermore, the government intends to digitize petition tracking, underscoring the growing importance of school meals in shaping education policy and ensuring accountability.

title: Steve Jobs once told Oracle founder Larry Ellison to not buy Apple
content: Larry Ellison planned to buy Apple for about five billion dollars then. Steve Jobs rejected this offer, preferring to return through NeXT. Jobs insisted on leading Apple from the moral high ground, not for financial gain. Ellison learned leadership from Jobs's decision to prioritize principles over profit. This choice ultimately led Apple to become the world's most valuable company.

title: Bengaluru has water reserves for only 4 months
content: Bengaluru's water supply is secure for the next four months. Reservoir storage levels are sufficient to meet the city's monthly water needs. Officials are monitoring groundwater and seeking reports on its status. Residents are urged to conserve water and avoid non-essential uses. Treated water should not be used for gardening or washing doorsteps.

title: Starship Flight 13 landed gently and floated for five days
content: SpaceX's Starship 40 achieved a successful splashdown landing in the Indian Ocean. The spacecraft remained intact and afloat for five days after its return. This marked a significant achievement for SpaceX's reusable rocket technology. Earlier Starship test flights experienced various failures and explosions upon landing. SpaceX is now sending a ship to recover the intact Starship 40.

title: Josh Allen’s charity golf event raises $17M; fatherhood deepens his empathy
content: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen now understands parents facing hospital crises more deeply.  His daughter Harper's birth has profoundly changed his perspective on children's health struggles.  Allen spoke emotionally at his "117 Holes for Charity" event, which supports Golisano Children's Hospital.  This fundraiser recently helped the Patricia Allen Fund reach seventeen million dollars in donations.  Fatherhood has reshaped Allen's priorities and his connection to the community.

title: Europe’s Big 4 can't stop making AI mistakes; PWC's report has ChatGPT as 'Source'
content: PwC's Middle East reports contained AI hallucinations and fabricated footnotes. Researchers found flawed citations and broken web links in several documents. Other Big Four firms like EY and KPMG also retracted AI-generated research papers. These incidents highlight challenges in marketing AI services while using generative tools. The firms are now reviewing their published research for accuracy.

title: From delivery rider to Rs 1 crore entrepreneur: How one accident changed his life
content: After financial hardship forced him to pause his medical studies, Ajit Kumar worked as a food delivery rider, cycling up to 100 kilometres daily to support his family. A serious road accident ended his delivery career but led him to discover writing through Pocket FM. Today, he is the lead writer of the hit audio-fiction series Brahmyodha: The Destroyer, has written over 1,000 episodes, and reportedly earned more than ₹1 crore through digital storytelling.

title: Will AI take your job? Cashiers to doctors, which professions face biggest risk
content: Artificial intelligence will automate routine jobs across many industries.  Complex tasks requiring human judgment will be supported by generative AI.  Financial services and retail trade see high automation risk for basic operations.  Healthcare and education will see AI strengthen clinical and learning roles.  Workplace tasks will be reshaped as AI complements human capabilities.

title: 'India ke liye ladne wala insaan': Tributes pour in as Ajinkya Rahane retires
content: Ajinkya Rahane represented India in 85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is. The Mumbai batter finished his Test career with 5,077 runs at an average of 38.46, including 12 centuries and 26 half-centuries. In ODIs, he scored 2,962 runs in 90 matches at an average of 35.26, with three centuries and 24 fifties. He also played 20 T20Is, scoring 375 runs.

title: UK announces £8.4 billion boost for Trident renewal under Dreadnought submarine programme
content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has unveiled new agreements for the Dreadnought submarine initiative. This crucial investment is projected to generate thousands of employment opportunities and apprenticeships within the defence industry. The modernization of the Trident nuclear deterrent is pivotal to the government's defence framework, aimed at replacing the outdated Vanguard-class submarines with enhanced vessels, reinforcing both national security and economic revival.

title: We are in India, be realistic, says HC, lifts curbs on hotel over 2 insects
content: The Bombay high court quashed a hotel's license suspension after finding minor hygiene issues.  A solitary finding of two insects did not justify the continued suspension of the license.  The court accepted the hotel's undertaking to maintain high sanitation standards.  The Food and Drug Administration's drive aims to improve food safety across Maharashtra.  The court appreciated the state and FDA actions in enforcing food safety laws.

title: US judges issue removal orders against 801 Indians in June
content: US immigration judges issued 801 removal orders for Indian nationals in June 2026. Nationwide deportation rulings accelerated significantly, with a nearly 30% increase in one month. This indicates a faster disposal of immigration cases by US courts. Indian migrants, many from Gujarat and Punjab, face sustained enforcement actions. The data shows immigration courts are disposing of cases at a much faster pace.

title: Bihar man beheads sister-in-law over delay in serving food, hangs head from tree

He then allegedly hung her severed head from a banyan tree near his home. Villagers discovered the gruesome scene and alerted the local police. The accused was apprehended by villagers and handed over to the authorities.

title: Suspect on FBI list died in Jalandhar road crash last year
content: Amritpal Singh, sought by the FBI, died in a road accident last year.  He had returned to his native village in Jalandhar from the US.  The FBI placed him on its wanted list for alleged involvement in a crime group.  This organization is accused of smuggling large quantities of cocaine and methamphetamine.  Federal authorities seized significant amounts of drugs and firearms during a major operation.

title: Made to share blanket with stranger on train, commission orders Railways to pay Rs 25,000
content: A consumer commission ordered Northern Railway to pay compensation to a passenger.  The passenger received only one blanket and pillow for a shared berth.  This action violated the railway's own circular regarding bedroll provisions.  The commission found the railways guilty of deficiency in service.  Compensation of twenty-five thousand rupees was awarded for inconvenience.

title: Mirabai Chanu’s education journey behind her Commonwealth glory
content: Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu’s journey shows that education extends beyond the classroom. While her demanding training limited traditional schooling, she pursued higher education through flexible learning while building resilience through real-life challenges. From carrying firewood in rural Manipur to overcoming Olympic heartbreak and injuries, Chanu transformed setbacks into strengths. Her perseverance culminated in a historic third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow 2026, highlighting the power of determination, continuous learning, and mental resilience.

title: Why electric cars may handle flooded roads better than petrol and diesel vehicles
content: Electric vehicles offer greater resilience in urban flooding situations.  Their sealed motors and battery packs prevent catastrophic engine damage common in petrol cars.  Modern EVs meet stringent waterproofing standards, minimizing electrical risks during waterlogged commutes.  While deep submersion poses risks for all vehicles, EVs are engineered to withstand typical flood conditions.  This engineering advantage makes them a more intelligent choice for India's changing weather patterns.

This initiative aims to boost the Garud unit's effectiveness across various mission profiles.
